scenario.title: Customers charged twice after checkout (reliability rehearsal, not an official contest problem)
scenario.initial_request: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

M-DUP-RATE.name: Share of orders with 2 captures per day

M-DUP-RETRY.name: Duplicate orders per gateway timeout retry

F-01.statement: Orders with 2 captures were 0 on 2026-09-07 and 2026-09-08, and equaled the gateway timeout retry count on 2026-09-09 (118) and 2026-09-10 (124).

F-02.statement: Change CHG-77 on 2026-09-09 by SH-PAY set idempotency_key_enforcement from on to off, noted as temporary for latency debugging; rollback_executed is false.

F-03.statement: Weekly double-charge tickets were 9 (W35) and 11 (W36), then 288 (W37) and 301 (W38), with weekly orders of about 20,500-21,400.

F-04.statement: On 2026-09-09..10, 242 duplicate orders were all gateway-timeout retries sent without an idempotency key. On 2026-09-01..08, 238 retries were sent with keys and deduplicated by the PSP, with 0 duplicates.

F-05.statement: Payments runbook section 4 allows automation to execute set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config only after SH-OPS confirms at runtime; the change is reversible.

F-06.statement: The charge ledger lists 4 open duplicate-capture orders (O-90211, O-90244, O-90302, O-90318), each with 2 captures and refunded=false.

CL-01.statement: Build an AI assistant that drafts apology replies to customers who complain about being charged twice

CL-02.statement: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

CL-03.statement: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

H-REPLY-DRAFTING-GAP.statement: The problem is that customer service replies to double-charge complaints are slow or poor, so an AI apology drafter solves it.

H-IDEMPOTENCY-DISABLED.statement: Idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries was disabled by a gateway configuration change, so retries create duplicate captures.

H-RETRY-LOGIC-DEFECT.statement: The checkout or capture retry logic sends repeat capture requests, for example on timeouts, with new keys even though enforcement is on. This is a defect in the H-CAPTURE handoff.

H-PSP-SIDE-DUPLICATION.statement: The PSP processes or logs a single capture request twice, so the duplicates originate on the PSP side.

H-PERCEIVED-DUPLICATE-NOT-REAL.statement: Many complaints are not true double captures. They may be a pending authorization plus a capture, or a display artifact, so the complaints overstate the actual duplicates.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Duplicate captures are real in the charge ledger and begin abruptly on 2026-09-09. Timeout retries were steady (117-124/day) throughout, but produced 0 duplicates on 09-07 and 09-08 and a duplicate for every retry on 09-09 and 09-10.
CHG-77 by SH-PAY on 2026-09-09 turned idempotency_key_enforcement from on to off, noted as temporary, with no rollback executed. This matches the abrupt onset of duplicate captures in E-01.

Double-charge tickets jumped from 9 and 11 per week (W35, W36) to 288 and 301 (W37, W38) while order volume stayed about 21,000 per week. The complaint surge is real and starts abruptly, which is consistent with a real duplicate-capture onset rather than a drafting or reply problem.

On 09-09..10 all 242 duplicate orders were gateway-timeout retries sent without an idempotency key, with none from other paths. On 09-01..08, 238 keyed retries were deduplicated by the PSP, giving 0 duplicates.

E-05.content: On 09-09 we switched idempotency-key enforcement off on the gateway to debug capture latency. It was meant to be temporary. Gateway timeouts and automatic capture retries have always happened at about the same rate; with the key the PSP drops the retried capture. Turning enforcement back on is a one-setting change through the gateway config tool, but payments operations has to confirm it at runtime.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The payments engineer states he switched idempotency-key enforcement off on 09-09 for latency debugging, intended as temporary. He says timeouts and retries occur at a steady rate, and that with the key the PSP drops retried captures. Re-enabling is a one-setting change that payments operations must confirm at runtime. This is a non-authoritative claim that agrees with E-02 and E-04.

E-06.content: Customers are furious about double charges. We just need faster, nicer apology replies.

E-07.content: Payments change runbook §4: the gateway operation set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after the payments operations manager SH-OPS confirms it at runtime. The change is reversible (setting can be switched back).

interpretation_history.interpretation: The runbook (E-07) states that set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config may be executed by automation only after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and that the change is reversible. This matches constraint K-GW.

U-LATENCY.question: Does re-enabling enforcement bring back the capture latency that SH-PAY was debugging?
U-LATENCY.decision_impact: Could require a follow-up or a different mitigation.

A-REENABLE-FIXES.statement: Re-enabling enforcement stops new duplicates without side effects such as the latency issue SH-PAY was debugging.

A-ALREADY-CHARGED.statement: Customers already double-charged still need refunds or reversals, which re-enabling does not provide.

problem_definition.requested_solution: Re-enable idempotency-key enforcement on capture retries (set_capture_idempotency) after payments operations manager runtime confirmation. Handle already-duplicated customers separately, rather than building an apology drafter as the remedy.
symptoms: Orders with 2 captures went from 0 on 09-07 and 09-08 to 118 on 09-09 and 124 on 09-10 (E-01).
Double-charge tickets rose from 9 and 11 per week to 288 and 301 per week (E-03).
problem_definition.root_problem: Customers are being double-charged because CHG-77 turned idempotency-key enforcement off on 2026-09-09, so gateway-timeout capture retries go to the PSP without a key and are processed as second captures (E-01, E-02, E-04). Falsifiable premise: re-enabling enforcement should drop duplicates to 0 while retries continue at about 120/day.

structural_remedies.description: Re-enable idempotency-key enforcement with set_capture_idempotency on gateway-config, after SH-OPS confirms at runtime. Then check that duplicates fall to 0 for 3 days while retries continue (SC-1).
structural_remedies.rationale: It is a one-setting reversible change (E-05, E-07). Authorization DA-SET-CAPTURE-IDEMPOTENCY is granted to SH-OPS, and K-GW requires runtime confirmation by SH-OPS. About 225 minutes remain.; residual gap: U-LATENCY is open, so the latency SH-PAY was debugging may return. The 3-day SC-1 window may extend beyond the contest time. Customers already double-charged are not fixed.

structural_remedies.description: Add a process rule that temporary config changes need an owner, an expiry and a rollback ticket. Add an alert on orders with 2 captures per gateway timeout retry (M-DUP-RETRY).
structural_remedies.rationale: A process or monitoring change is allowed. It needs ownership decisions and cannot be fully built and validated in the remaining time, so it is a proposal for follow-up.; residual gap: It does not stop the current duplicates. It only prevents recurrence.

structural_remedies.description: Quantify outstanding duplicate captures in DA-CHG (VOB-U-REFUNDS). Then refund or reverse them through the existing payments process, owned by payments operations.
structural_remedies.rationale: The charge ledger can be read (payments-db is healthy). The quantification is read-only, and refunds go through the existing ownership. No refund tool is in the tool surface, so refunds are not executed by automation.; residual gap: The refund count is unknown (U-REFUNDS). Refund execution is outside the listed tools.

proposal.summary: The request was an AI apology drafter, but the evidence shows a different problem. CHG-77 turned idempotency-key enforcement off on 2026-09-09, so gateway-timeout retries went out without a key and became second captures (E-01, E-02, E-04). The release decision is HOLD. Re-enabling enforcement is the proposed fix, but it has not been confirmed as executed or verified. The H-CAPTURE handoff is still unverified, and Layer 1 verification failed.
key_points: Duplicate captures began abruptly on 2026-09-09. Orders with 2 captures went from 0 on 09-07 and 09-08 to 118 on 09-09 and 124 on 09-10, while retries held steady at about 120 a day (E-01).
CHG-77 by SH-PAY on 2026-09-09 turned idempotency_key_enforcement from on to off, and no rollback was executed (E-02). SH-PAY's own account agrees (E-05).
All 242 duplicate orders on 09-09..10 were timeout retries sent without a key. From 09-01..08, 238 keyed retries were deduplicated by the PSP (E-04).

Double-charge tickets rose from 9 and 11 per week to 288 and 301 per week (E-03). This points to a real duplicate-capture problem rather than a reply-drafting problem. The hypotheses H-REPLY-DRAFTING-GAP, H-PSP-SIDE-DUPLICATION, H-RETRY-LOGIC-DEFECT and H-PERCEIVED-DUPLICATE-NOT-REAL were rejected.
The runbook allows set_capture_idempotency only after SH-OPS confirms at runtime, and the change is reversible (E-07, K-GW). No pending protected action is recorded in the state.
The charge ledger shows 4 open duplicate-capture orders with no refund: O-90211, O-90244, O-90302 and O-90318 (E-08).
HOLD reasons: the H-CAPTURE handoff is semantically unverified, and Layer 1 verification failed on handoff_delivery_semantic.
limitations_explained: The H-CAPTURE handoff delivery and semantic validity are unknown, so the re-enable cannot be shown to work end to end. The retry-key check (W-WI-VERIFY-KEYS) is still pending, and no catalog operation exists for it.

The success criteria are not yet met. SC-1 needs 0 duplicates per day for 3 consecutive days after the re-enable, and that window may run past the contest time. The state has no post-change evidence for SC-1 or SC-2.

Customers who were already double-charged are not fixed by the re-enable (A-ALREADY-CHARGED). Refund execution is outside the tool surface, and the 4 open orders in E-08 need payments operations to handle them.
U-LATENCY is open, so the capture latency SH-PAY was debugging may return after the re-enable. A-REENABLE-FIXES, which says re-enabling has no side effects, is an unverified assumption.

The change-control guard (SR-CHANGE-CONTROL-GUARD) is not built. It would require an owner, an expiry and a rollback ticket for temporary config changes, plus an alert on M-DUP-RETRY, so a similar change could recur.
The DEFINE gate was only CONDITIONAL_PASS. The configuration audit log and the support tickets have unknown completeness (DA-CFG, DA-TKT), and the gateway-config tool health is UNKNOWN.
